pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read the account and identify what happened and what is still unknown
pages.subject: The neighbourhood post
paragraphs: A neighbourhood post claims that the café has closed permanently. It includes a photograph of a notice on the door, but it does not quote the owner or identify a staff member as its source.

A reply suggests that staffing problems caused the closure. The person replying gives no evidence for that explanation. The photograph shows that there is a notice; it does not, on its own, verify the claims in the post.

pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read the account and identify what happened and what is still unknown
pages.subject: The café’s notice
paragraphs: The café’s own notice says that the dining area is closed for renovation. Delivery orders are still being accepted. Customers are directed to the café’s own updates for further information.
No reopening date is given. The notice does not say that the business is closing permanently, and it makes no statement about staffing.

pages.title: Check what the source confirms

pages.title: Build passive reporting structures
pages.instruction: Use reporting passives to attribute a claim and mark whether its event is earlier

rows.subject: A reported clause
rows.verb: It is reported / said that + clause
rows.example: It is reported that the dining area is closed

rows.subject: A current reported situation
rows.verb: subject + is reported / said to + base verb
rows.example: The dining area is reported to be closed

rows.subject: An earlier reported event
rows.verb: subject + is reported / said to have + past participle
rows.example: The café is reported to have closed its dining area

pages.note: To have + participle places the reported event before the reporting time. A reporting structure attributes a claim; it does not make an unsupported claim true.

pages.message: Hi, Ana. The source has clarified the café notice. The dining area is closing for renovation, and delivery will continue, but a reopening date has not been set. The earlier post’s claim of permanent closure is not supported by the official notice. Could you revise the update with that attribution intact?
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana. The source has clarified the café notice. The dining area is closing for renovation, and delivery will continue, but a reopening date has not been set. The earlier post’s claim of permanent closure is not supported by the official notice. Could you revise the update with that attribution intact?
pages.greeting: Here’s another example of checking a claim before passing it on

items.prompt: Which source should anchor the revised update?
items.answer: The revised update should be attributed to the café’s official notice
A reopening date has not been set

items.prompt: What is the useful next step for someone planning a visit?
items.answer: They should check the café’s own updates rather than repeat the unverified post

additionalAudios.audioText: Please don’t replace the false certainty with a confident reopening date. If people need to plan a visit, the useful next step is to check the café’s own updates rather than repeat the same unverified post. We can explain what the notice confirms and what it leaves open without implying that every part of the original rumour has been investigated independently.

pages.title: When the source changes
pages.instruction: Assess the evidence behind Scott’s claim, then give a careful update

video.title: I was wrong (and so was everyone)

items.prompt: What did Scott’s earlier video claim about uninsured buildings?
items.hint: Report the story he repeated; do not present it as an established fact
items.answer: His earlier video claimed firefighters would let uninsured buildings burn

items.prompt: Which source made the claim seem trustworthy?
items.hint: Listen after the examples from television programmes
items.answer: He had used the history page on the London Fire Brigade Museum’s own website as one of his sources

items.prompt: What does the museum’s revised page change about the evidence?
items.hint: Distinguish a weaker evidence base from proof that every part of the story is false
items.answer: The revised page says there is little real evidence for the story. That weakens the support for presenting it as an established fact and makes further investigation necessary; this excerpt does not settle the whole historical question

items.prompt: Update a colleague: name the source and keep the uncertainty clear
items.hint: Use according to, was said to, or is now reported to. Make the correction clear without inventing a final conclusion
items.answer: Example: I repeated the story from the museum’s website. It now says there is little real evidence, so I would qualify the claim rather than present it as settled fact

s_mission.title: Post versus notice

questions.prompt: Which part of the café is closed, and why?
questions.answer: The dining area is closed for renovation.
questions.hint: Use the café’s notice rather than the neighbourhood post.

questions.answer: Delivery orders are still being accepted.
questions.hint: Find the service that continues during renovation.

questions.prompt: Who suggested that staff shortages caused the closure?
questions.answer: Another reader suggested it; the café did not.
questions.hint: Check the source of the reply in paragraph two.

referenceParagraphs: A neighbourhood post says the café has closed permanently. The café’s own notice says that only the dining area is closed for renovation and that delivery orders are still being accepted.
The notice gives no reopening date and says nothing about staffing. A reply blaming staff shortages comes from another reader, not from the café.

s_reply.title: The corrected update

questions.prompt: Which claim did the update correct?
questions.answer: It corrected the claim that the café had closed permanently.
questions.hint: Find the claim replaced in the first paragraph.
Find the service retained in the corrected update.

questions.prompt: Where should customers check for a reopening announcement?
questions.answer: They should check the café’s own updates.
questions.hint: Find the source given to customers planning a visit.

referenceParagraphs: The corrected update cites the café’s own notice. It replaces the claim of permanent closure with the confirmed reason: the dining area is closed for renovation. It also states that delivery continues.
The café has not announced a reopening date. Customers who want to visit the dining area are directed to the café’s own updates before making the journey.
